title: Definition

label: def:class
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:class}
For $1\le m\le d$, the class of multi-index functions is
\[
    \mathbb{F}_{m,d}(\boldsymbol{\beta},L)=\big\{F:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}\ \big|\ F(x)=f(\Theta x),\ \Theta\in\mathcal{V}_{m,d},\ f\in\mathbb{H}_m(\boldsymbol{\beta},L)\big\}.
\]
head: environment

title: Assumptions
body_md: In \eqref{eq:model}, $(X_i,\varepsilon_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$, are independent copies of $(X,\varepsilon)$, where $X$ and $\varepsilon$ are independent, $\varepsilon$ has a density $p$, and $X$ has a density $g$.
head: manual

label: ass:noise
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:noise}
The density $p$ is positive on $\mathbb{R}$, and there exist $q,Q>0$ such that
\[
    \int_\mathbb{R} \frac{p(y+\upsilon_1)\,p(y+\upsilon_2)}{p(y)}\,\mathrm{d} y\le 1+Q|\upsilon_1\upsilon_2|\qquad\forall\,\upsilon_1,\upsilon_2\in[-q,q].
\]
head: environment

label: ass:design
title: Assumption
body_md:
\label{ass:design}
There exists $\mathfrak{g}>0$ such that, for every $k\in\{1,\ldots,d\}$ and every $O\in\mathcal{V}_{k,d}$, the random vector $OX$ has a density bounded by $\mathfrak{g}$.
head: environment

label: th:m<d
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:m<d}
Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:noise} and~\ref{ass:design} hold, $d\ge 2$, $1\le m<d$, $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in(0,\infty)^m$, $L>0$, $r\ge1$ and $t\in\mathbb{R}^d$. There exists $\varkappa>0$ independent of $n$ and $L$ such that, for all $n$ large enough,
\[
    \inf_{\tilde F}\ \sup_{F\in\mathbb{F}_{m,d}(\boldsymbol{\beta},L)}\mathcal{R}^{(n)}_{r,t}\big(\tilde F,F\big)\ \ge\ \varkappa\,\psi_n(\gamma,L),
\]
where the infimum is taken over all estimators.
head: environment
name: Dimension reduction, $m<d$

label: th:m=d
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{th:m=d}
Let Assumptions~\ref{ass:noise} and~\ref{ass:design} hold, $d\ge2$, $L>0$, $r\ge 1$, $t\in\mathbb{R}^d$, and let $\boldsymbol{\beta}\in(0,\infty)^d$ have at least two distinct components. Then there exists $\varkappa>0$ independent of $n$ and $L$ such that, for all $n$ large enough,
\[
    \inf_{\tilde F}\ \sup_{F\in\mathbb{F}_{d,d}(\boldsymbol{\beta},L)}\mathcal{R}^{(n)}_{r,t}\big(\tilde F,F\big)\ \ge\ \varkappa\,\psi_n(\gamma,L).
\]
head: environment
name: No dimension reduction, $m=d$

label: prop:iso
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:iso}
Let $\beta\in(0,1]$ and $L>0$. Then
\[
    \mathbb{H}_d(\beta,L)\subset\mathbb{F}_{d,d}(\beta,L)\subset\mathbb{H}_d\big(\beta,d^{\,1-\beta/2}L\big).
\]
Consequently, for fixed $\beta$ and $L$ the pointwise minimax rates over $\mathbb{F}_{d,d}(\beta,L)$ and over $\mathbb{H}_d(\beta,L)$ coincide up to constant factors. In particular, whenever $n^{-\beta/(2\beta+d)}$ is the minimax rate over $\mathbb{H}_d(\beta,L)$ (for instance, under the standard conditions of \citealp{Stone80}, including a design density bounded away from zero near $t$), it is also the minimax rate over $\mathbb{F}_{d,d}(\beta,L)$, and no logarithmic factor appears.
head: environment
name: Isotropic link, $m=d$

title: Remark
body_md: In terms of the dimension, Theorems~\ref{th:m<d} and~\ref{th:m=d} agree with Stone's dimensionality reduction principle: the rate is that of an $m$-dimensional anisotropic problem, the dimension being hidden in $\gamma$, up to the factor $(\ln n)^{\gamma/(2\gamma+1)}$. In the isotropic case $\boldsymbol{\beta}=(\beta,\ldots,\beta)$ with $m<d$, Theorem~\ref{th:m<d} reads $\psi_n=L^{m/(2\beta+m)}(n^{-1}\ln n)^{\beta/(2\beta+m)}$; here the logarithm is present for every $\beta$, since a function of $m<d$ variables is never rotation invariant in $\mathbb{R}^d$.
head: environment

label: rem:mechanism
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:mechanism}
In the proofs, the hypotheses are bumps of height $\asymp\psi_n$ with widths $h_k$ along the rows of $\Theta$, where $h_k$ is smaller in the directions of lower smoothness, and they differ only by rotations through angles of order $N^{-1}$. Two bumps with widths $h_1<h_2$ in a plane, rotated by an angle $\phi$, overlap roughly in proportion $h_1/(h_2\phi)$. When $h_1/h_2$ is polynomially small in $n$, a polynomial number $N=n^b$ of rotated bumps is almost orthogonal, while the Kullback--Leibler divergence between each of them and $F_0\equiv0$ may be as large as a multiple of $\ln N\asymp\ln n$; this produces the logarithm. If $h_1=h_2$, rotations do not separate the hypotheses, which is why Proposition~\ref{prop:iso} holds. For $m<d$ the role of $h_2$ is played by the infinite width of the ridge function in the directions orthogonal to the rows of $\Theta$.
head: environment
name: Mechanism

label: rem:iso-beta
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:iso-beta}
Proposition~\ref{prop:iso} is stated for $\beta\le 1$, where it follows from an elementary argument. For $\beta>1$ the class $\mathbb{H}_d(\beta,L)$ in Definition~\ref{def:holder} controls only the pure partial derivatives, and the analogous inclusion requires embedding theorems for anisotropic H\"older--Nikol'skii spaces \citep{Nikolskii75}; we do not pursue this here.
